name: MattermostMCP Local Server Startup
observations: Environment: Windows repo accessed from WSL Ubuntu-22.04 at /mnt/c/Users/user/source/repos/MattermostMCP. Use pwsh.exe (Windows PowerShell 7) for the PowerShell scripts via WSL interop.
Docker daemon is NOT installed/available. Only docker-compose.exe (v2.23.3) and podman.exe exist. Use podman as the compose engine.
Step 1: start the podman VM: `pwsh.exe -NoProfile -Command "podman machine start"`. Docker API forwarding fails but podman clients work. If needed `podman machine init` first.

Step 2: bring up the stack: `pwsh.exe -NoProfile -File scripts/mattermost-server-preview.ps1 -ComposeEngine podman` (or mattermost-server-start.ps1 which also runs prepare). Images mattermost-preview:local and postgres:15-alpine already exist.

Step 3: seed team/channel/users: `pwsh.exe -NoProfile -File scripts/prepare.ps1 -ComposeEngine podman` (idempotent: test-team, test-channel, admin@example.com, testuser@example.com, password ChangeMe123!).

PITFALL: the mattermost/mattermost-preview image ALWAYS starts its own internal PostgreSQL 12 on 5432 (data in an anonymous podman volume, DB name mattermost_test). This races with the compose `postgres:15` service (host network, ./data/postgres, DB mattermost). If the internal PG wins, postgres:15 exits (Address already in use) and Mattermost fails with 'database "mattermost" does not exist'.

FIX for the 5432 conflict: `podman stop mattermost`, `podman start mattermost-postgres`, wait for it to bind 5432, then `podman start mattermost`. The internal PG then fails to bind (harmless) and Mattermost connects to the external postgres with DB mattermost.
Verify Mattermost: `curl http://localhost:8080/api/v4/system/ping` -> {"status":"OK"}. WSL uses mirrored networking so localhost:8080 works from WSL and Windows.

Step 4: start the MCP server from WSL: `setsid bash -c 'dotnet run --project src/McpServer --launch-profile McpServer.Local > /tmp/opencode/mcpserver.log 2>&1 < /dev/null' < /dev/null &`. Uses ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Local, listens on http://127.0.0.1:8085.

MCP verify: POST http://127.0.0.1:8085/mcp with tools/call mattermost_list_followed_threads returns followed threads. REST /api/threads/* returns 401 (requires auth) even in Local; the MCP /mcp endpoint works without auth in Local.
BaseUrl in src/McpServer/appsettings.Local.json is http://localhost:8080; DeveloperUserName=testuser.

Test projects live under test/: nextorm.core.tests (unit, 82 tests), nextorm.integration.tests (307 tests: shared suite over InMemory/Postgres/SqlServer), plus nextorm.postgres.tests, nextorm.sqlserver.tests, nextorm.sqlite.tests.

Build policy: TreatWarningsAsErrors=true is set globally in Directory.Build.props (applies to every project and every configuration). Build is expected to be 0 warnings / 0 errors; fix warnings or add explicit NoWarn, never leave them.

To enable TreatWarningsAsErrors, 5 pre-existing CS8602 warnings were fixed by making the null guards unconditional: (1) ResultSetEnumerator.cs InitReader/InitReaderAsync had _conn/_dbContext null checks wrapped in #if DEBUG, so Release lost the narrowing; checks are now unconditional. (2) QueryCommand.cs ReplaceCommand had the _referencedQueries null check inside #if DEBUG; now unconditional while the _dataContext equality check stays Debug-only.
Verified after enabling TreatWarningsAsErrors: Release and Debug builds 0 warnings / 0 errors; nextorm.core.tests 82/82; nextorm.integration.tests 307 total / 0 failed / 1 intentional skip.

Perf findings live in /mnt/c/Users/user/source/repos/nextorm/performance-findings.md (untracked). The 'Сводка находок' table now has a 'Статус' column: M1 blue (closed, not a bug), M2 done (sync), M3/M4/M9/M10/M11 not started, M5-M8 done, I1 partial (via M8), I2-I6 not started.

M1 was reclassified after review: on a QueryPlanCache hit the SQL is NOT rebuilt (GetPreparedQueryCommand returns the cached DbPreparedQueryCommand). The per-call cost is the builder path: Where() rebuilds the expression, ToCommand() allocates a fresh QueryCommand, and GetAnyCommand runs a full PrepareCommand (clause walks + *PlanHash) because the command is fresh. Measured: builder 2.25 KB/1.65us, full public path 2.76 KB/13us, prepared reuse 0.87 KB/12us. Conclusion: use Prepare()/IPreparedQueryCommand; remaining levers are memoizing the prepared command on the Entity instance and removing per-call QueryPlan/QueryPlanCacheKey allocations.

M2 final API design (user waived compat): public sync API is M() (exact parameterless overload, required because a params ReadOnlySpan call site is rejected inside expression trees: CS8640 + CS9226, even with zero args) plus M(params ReadOnlySpan<object?>) which covers every arity with no heap array. No params object[] left on the sync surface; async/streaming keep params object[] because the array is stored in ResultSetEnumerator and must survive await. Measured: 1 arg -32 B, 3 args -48 B per call.

M5-M8 implemented and verified (build Release+Debug 0 warnings/0 errors with TreatWarningsAsErrors; core 82/82; integration 307/0 failed via Podman). Micro-benchmark MicroOptimizationsBenchmark.cs shows: M7 StartsWith culture 10.4ns -> ~0ns and EndsWith 13.5ns -> ~0ns (the real win, runs on every plan build); M8 string.Format('norm_p{0}',7) 35.2ns+64B -> 0.21ns+0B (param-name cache in DbContext.GetParamName; IndexOf amortized by ParamMap so it is first-call only); M5 Convert.ToBoolean(long) 0.182->0.150ns and M6 HasFlag 1.204->1.176ns are within noise (the original 'boxing' claim was wrong).
M10-M11 implemented (build Release+Debug 0 warnings/0 errors; core 82/82; integration 307/0 failed/1 skip via Podman).

M10 (sealing): sealed added to ResultSetEnumerator<TResult>, InMemoryEnumerator<TResult,TEntity>, InMemoryCompiledQuery<TResult,TEntity>, QueryCommand<TResult>. Cannot seal Entity<TEntity> (EntityP2/P3 derive) or PreparedQueryCommand (DbPreparedQueryCommand/InMemoryCompiledQuery derive). Two knock-on fixes were required: ResultSetEnumerator.Dispose(bool) protected virtual -> private, and the protected ctor of QueryCommand<TResult> -> private (CS0628 under TreatWarningsAsErrors). Honest finding: the M10 micro-benchmark arm shows NO measurable gain (30.75 vs 30.82 ns) because tiered PGO already devirtualizes monomorphic interface calls; sealing is a structural change, not a measured speedup. Kept, but offered to revert if minimal public API matters.

M11 (LINQ in plan/map build): replaced 4 LINQ sites in DbContext with loops: (1) @params.Any(it => !IsRuntimeParam(it.Name)) -> early-exit loop; (2) Parameters.AddRange(params.Select(CreateParam).ToArray()) -> loop of Parameters.Add; (3) SelectList.Select(MapColumnExpression).ToArray() -> new Expression[n] + loop; (4) SelectList.Select(Expression.Bind).ToArray() -> new MemberBinding[n] + loop. Micro-benchmark: Any(pred) 2.67 -> 2.06 ns; Select().ToArray() 24.71 ns + 120 B -> 9.87 ns + 48 B (-72 B). The path is cold (plan-cache miss / map-cache miss, once per query shape per thread), so no steady-state effect.

Remaining findings M3/M4/M9 + I1-I6 completed on branch 1.0.3-alpha. Verification: Release+Debug builds 0 warnings/0 errors (TreatWarningsAsErrors); nextorm.core.tests 84/84; nextorm.integration.tests 307 total / 0 failed / 1 skip via Podman (Postgres+SQL Server+sqlite).

M3: ResultSetEnumerator.MoveNextAsync is no longer async on the hot path - calls reader.ReadAsync(ct) and when task.IsCompletedSuccessfully reads+maps synchronously; async continuation only for genuinely async reads; cold init path in InitReaderAndMoveNextAsync. Micro-bench (100 rows): 690.0 ns -> 108.4 ns (-5.8 ns/row, 6.4x), zero allocations in both variants (async ValueTask<T> does not box on synchronous completion).

M4: QueryCommand.Pipeline rewritten - removed Task.Run(ToEnumerable) + Channel.CreateUnbounded. Now: await using var enumerator = CreateAsyncEnumerator(...); while (await enumerator.MoveNextAsync()) yield return enumerator.Current; with [EnumeratorCancellation]. Removed CS8425 pragma and 'using System.Threading.Channels'. Tests: TestFetch now asserts 100 rows + content; new TestFetch_PipelineStopsOnCancellation asserts early stop (seen == 10).

M9: ExpressionPlanEqualityComparer.GetHashCode used a shared mutable Visitor (_visitor._hash) while comparers are cached on QueryCommand including the shared AnyCommand -> torn hashes across threads. Fixed with [ThreadStatic] _tlsVisitor + _tlsVisitorOwner (one visitor per thread per comparer, still lazy/zero-extra-alloc). Evidence: new regression test GetHashCode_ShouldBeThreadSafe (8 expressions x 50,000 Parallel.For calls vs single-threaded baseline) - with [ThreadStatic] temporarily removed it fails with 49,971/50,000 mismatched hashes; with fix 0. Also CompareLambda no longer throws InvalidOperationException on a TryAdd collision (same ParameterExpression in a nested lambda), returns false instead.

Known-but-unfixed (reported in performance-findings.md): GetAnyCommand uses ReplaceCommand to mutate the shared cached AnyCommand, so concurrent use of one DbContext can let different predicates see the wrong plan. Correctness issue, needs AnyCommand to become per-call; out of scope.

I1: string.Format removed from all real sites - BaseExpressionVisitor.cs:158 now uses DbContext.GetParamName (M8 cached norm_pN table), DefaultParamProvider.GetParamName uses a growing static pN cache, SqlServerDbContext.MakeTop uses $"top({limit})" (interpolation of int does not box). I2: InMemoryDataContext map-build LINQ -> loops. I3: 19 ToList/ToArray left (was 27), all cold (joins?.ToArray() snapshot only when joins exist, CloneForCache, MakeGenericType). I4: verified by code that all Expression.Compile() are under DataContextCache.ExpressionsCache / MapperCache (one-time per expression). I5: LogCommand uses DbContext._sbPool StringBuilder + object[] instead of StringBuilder+ArrayList+interpolation, same log text. I6: 32 .ToString(), zero in per-row materializer.
performance-findings.md: all M1-M11 and I1-I6 rows now have statuses; sections M3, M4, M9 and an I1-I6 review table added. Benchmarks: M3 arms added to MicroOptimizationsBenchmark.cs.

Benchmark methodology caveats for this repo's ShortRun config (Job.ShortRun = warmup 3 / iterations 3 + InProcessEmitToolchain, the default; NEXTORM_BENCH_FULL=1 switches to Job.Default out-of-process): it cannot resolve 1-2 ns effects - 16 of 129 methods had Error > Mean and ~50 had >20%. BDN also fails to raise process priority in WSL ('Failed to set up priority High ... Permission denied') and GC is Concurrent Workstation. Absolute micro values drift ~30% between sessions while RATIOS stay stable (M3: 690->108 ns previously vs 480->83 ns now, i.e. ~6x both times) - compare ratios, not absolutes. BenchmarkQueryCommand.ExpressionPlanEqualityComparer (190.3 ns +- 597.4 ns) is unusable and needs a full run.

Benchmark verdicts from the full run: CONFIRMED - M3 (479.9->82.6 ns, 5.8x, 0 alloc), M7 Ordinal (14.57->0.005 ns StartsWith, 19.31->0.008 ns EndsWith; JIT folds it away, 0.005 ns is the measurement floor), M8 (47.48 ns + 64 B -> 0.257 ns + 0 B, 185x), M11 (Any 2.914->2.011 ns -31%; SelectToArray 19.89/120B -> 9.16/48B -54%). MARGINAL - M6 HasFlag->bitwise (2.233->1.699 ns, -24%, but error 13-21%). NOISE - M5 (-2%) and M10 sealed/devirtualization (-1%, second run in a row with no effect; recommendation to revert stands). M2 gives exactly -32 B per public-API call (EntityAny 2832->2800 B) and -3200 B at the GetDbCommand layer, with time inside the noise. Note the ParamsAllocationBenchmark 'Generic_ParamsArray' arm shows 0 B allocated because params object[] with zero args is Array.Empty, so that arm does not measure allocation at all.

Product-level results (Nextorm_Prepared vs best competitor): Any 943.2us/85.2KB vs Dapper 1401.8/139.1 (1.49x); Iteration 10.78us/976B vs Dapper 15.83/1904 (1.47x); First scalar 94.8/8.6 vs Dapper 146.9/16.5 (1.55x); Single 95.1/8.4 vs Dapper 148.5/16.4 (1.56x); Join 109.5/12.3 vs Dapper 201.7/21.5 (1.84x); Where 942.3/92.4 vs Dapper 1385.0/180.7 (1.47x); SimulateWork 7.003ms/6.24MB vs Dapper 25.836/8.9 (3.69x); LargeIteration 9.10ms/2.21MB vs Ado 9.76/2.68 (1.07x, I/O-bound - all impls converge at 8.6-14.7 ms, so micro-optimizations there are pointless). Benchmark repo hygiene issues found: SqliteBenchmarkMakeSelect.cs and ExpressionsExperiments.cs have ALL [Benchmark] attributes commented out, so --filter "*" silently skips them (161 cases actually run vs 227 counted by grep of '[Benchmark' which also matches comments). SqliteBenchmarkCachedPlan.cs uses [HideColumns(..., Column.Error, Column.StdDev)] which hides whether its deltas are significant. M5/M6/M7/M8/M10 and BenchmarkQueryCommand need NEXTORM_BENCH_FULL=1 or IterationCount 10-15.

M12 CORRECTED (my first version of M12 was WRONG - important lesson). Measured on 2026-09-16 with a clean full run (`NEXTORM_BENCH_FULL=1 ./nextorm.benchmark --filter "*SqliteBenchmarkCachedPlan*"`, Job.Default out-of-process, errors 2-4%): the ranking is explicit Prepare() (11.94 us/call, 0.76 KB) -> implicit plan cache (17.56 us, 3.76 KB, ratio 1.47) -> cache DISABLED via QueryCommand.Cache = false (42.06 us, 5.49 KB, ratio 3.52). So the plan cache is 2.4x BETTER than no cache, not worse. My first M12 concluded the opposite ('cache does not pay for itself') because I compared a plan-only arm (Build_Sql 4.54 us) against end-to-end cached overhead (5.32 us) instead of measuring the actual no-cache alternative. Recommendation 'remove the cache' is RETRACTED.

M12 corrected decomposition (SqliteBenchmarkCachedPlan, 100-iteration loops, full run, per call): Construct_Only 1.12 us/1.68 KB; RePrepare_PlanOnly_Param 1.63 us/0.78 KB; Cached_PlanOnly_NoParam 2.77 us/2.66 KB; Cached_PlanOnly_Param 3.56 us/3.00 KB (ExtractParams delta 0.79 us); Build_Sql 5.09 us/4.54 KB/Gen1 0.51; M12_NoCache_PlanOnly_Param 5.36 us/4.55 KB/Gen1 0.53; Build_Sql_Join 14.25 us/11.52 KB/Gen1 0.86; Prepared_ToList 11.94 us/0.76 KB; Cached_ToList 17.56 us/3.76 KB; M12_NoCache_ToList 42.06 us/5.49 KB/Gen1 0.47. Model checks out: construct 1.12 + (prepare+hash+lookup) 1.63 = 2.75 ~ 2.77 = Cached_PlanOnly_NoParam. Composition of the 3.56 us cache-hit path: 31% command construction, 46% prepare+*PlanHash+lookup, 22% ExtractParams. Cache disabled produces Gen1 on every call (0.47-0.53) because DbCommand+CreateParameter are rebuilt; the cached path produces 0 Gen1.

M12 root cause and the right lever: the expensive part is that PrepareCommand computes every *PlanHash by a FULL expression-tree walk on every call (QueryCommand.cs:541 and the analogous blocks in PrepareColumns/PrepareJoin/PrepareSorting/PrepareGrouping; PrepareCommand(bool dontCalculateHash, ct) is called as PrepareCommand(!storeInCache, ct) at DbContext.cs:303, and the public implicit path always passes storeInCache:true so dontCalculateHash=false). _dontCache gates those hashes together with the lookup - which is why Cache=false removes hashing AND caching and is net slower. Correct lever is what M1 originally recommended: use Prepare()/IPreparedQueryCommand (1.47x faster, 4.94x fewer allocations than implicit cache). Do NOT disable the cache. Per-instance hash memoization will not help because Entity.Where() builds a fresh tree each call. Removing per-call QueryPlan/QueryPlanCacheKey is ~2% (the object is ~50 B of 3.00 KB/call) - not a priority.

M1 history nuance (owner feedback, final corrected form): the plan cache was implemented, then REMOVED BY THE OWNER as too expensive ('sometimes it is faster without the cache'), then re-added after my M1 conclusion 'this is not a cache bug'. The measured result: the owner's 'faster without cache' experience corresponds to using an explicitly PREPARED command, not to disabling the cache - disabling it is 3.52x slower. So M1's mechanical claim was right (SQL is not rebuilt on a cache-hit) and M1's own secondary recommendation (use Prepare()) turned out to be the real win, but my phrasing 'not a cache bug' was too permissive and led to reading it as 'the cache is useful'. M1 is now marked 'reopened -> M12' and M12 is corrected.

Benchmark arms added to SqliteBenchmarkCachedPlan.cs to settle M12 (kept): M12_NoCache_PlanOnly_Param (construct + Cache=false + GetPreparedQueryCommand, no DB) and M12_NoCache_ToList (end-to-end with Cache=false), plus Column.Error/Column.StdDev were un-hidden from [HideColumns] so significance is visible. These two arms are the decisive measurement and should be re-run before any cache-related change.

Docs: created docs/prepared-vs-cached.md (English, matching readme.md/docs/index.md) - the user-facing reference for the two reuse paths. Contents: comparison table (entry point, lookup key, lifetime, scope, cache population, per-call cost, thread-safety, streamability), how the implicit plan cache works (key/value, hit criteria, per-call cost breakdown, parameter rules), how Prepare() works (nonStreamUsing, storeInCache:false consequences), choosing guidance, known problems, reproduction commands. Linked from readme.md (Features bullet) and docs/index.md (new 'Query reuse' section before 'Releases').

Plan-cache semantics established while writing docs/prepared-vs-cached.md: _queryPlanCache is [ThreadStatic] static (DbContext.cs:40-41) so it is per-thread and shared by ALL IDataContext instances on that thread; the key is (Type ContextType, QueryPlan) so providers do not collide. Per-thread-ness is why the shared mutable DbCommand is safe, and it also means thread-pool hopping loses cache hits. Entries live until PurgeQueryCache() (DbContext.cs:1202) - there is NO automatic invalidation, so schema changes require a manual purge. Dispose() iterates all cached entries on the thread and calls ResetConnection when the context owns the connection (DbContext.cs:697-716), so cached commands outlive their context. The stored key is QueryPlan.GetCacheVersion() (clone via QueryCommand.CloneForCache) so caller mutation cannot corrupt it. Runtime params are named norm_p{index} (IsRuntimeParam, DbContext.cs:174); on a hit values are refreshed only when NeedsParamRefresh; ParamMap memoises parameters.IndexOf. QueryCommand.Cache=false disables hashing AND lookup and is a 3.52x regression - not a tuning knob.

Prepare() semantics: QueryCommand.Prepare(bool nonStreamUsing = true, ct) => GetPreparedQueryCommand(this, !nonStreamUsing, storeInCache: false, ct) (QueryCommand.cs:810); Entity.Prepare => ToCommand().Prepare(...) (Entity.cs:379). storeInCache:false means it never populates the plan cache AND is passed as dontCalculateHash:true, so no *PlanHash is computed - that is the whole 1.47x/4.94x win. nonStreamUsing:true (default) creates no ResultSetEnumerator and is buffered/scalar only (streaming NRE, verified by test); nonStreamUsing:false supports streaming. Terminal methods take the IDataContext as first arg (prepared command is not bound to one context, but IS bound to the provider representation: DbContext.AsDbCommand throws ArgumentException on a mismatch). A prepared command owns ONE mutable DbCommand and ONE ResultSetEnumerator, so it must not be shared across threads nor used for two overlapping iterations.

BUG FIXED (2026-09-16): the cache-hit branch of DbContext.GetPreparedQueryCommand ignored createEnumerator (the block was commented out), so a query shape first executed with a buffered terminal (createEnumerator:false - ToList/ToListAsync/First/Single/ExecuteScalar) was cached WITHOUT a ResultSetEnumerator and a later streaming call on the same shape (ToAsyncEnumerable / ToEnumerable) dereferenced compiledQuery.Enumerator! and threw NullReferenceException. Both async (DbContext.CreateAsyncEnumerator) and sync (DbContext.CreateEnumerator) were affected. Fix applied in the hit branch, replacing the commented-out block: `if (createEnumerator && compiledQuery.Enumerator is null) compiledQuery.Enumerator = new ResultSetEnumerator<TResult>(compiledQuery);` The plan cache is [ThreadStatic] so the entry is only touched by its owning thread (no race), and buffered calls pass createEnumerator:false so the condition short-circuits - zero hot-path cost. The in-memory provider was never affected: InMemoryDataContext.CreateAsyncEnumerator builds a fresh enumerator per call instead of using a stored field.

Test file test/nextorm.sqlite.tests/PlanCacheTests.cs now has 6 tests, 0 skipped, all against a real temp-file SQLite db (file, not ':memory:', because ':memory:' is per-connection): BufferedThenAsyncStreaming_OnTheSameShape_ShouldNotThrow and BufferedThenSyncStreaming_OnTheSameShape_ShouldNotThrow (both failed with NRE before the fix, now regression tests), Prepared_Default_ShouldNotBeStreamable (pins the documented buffered-only contract as an NRE), Prepared_NonStreaming_ShouldSupportStreaming, Prepared_Default_ShouldBeBufferedAndReusable, Prepared_ShouldNotPopulateThePlanCache. Gotchas: IDataContext.Create<T> is a default interface method so the context must be typed as IDataContext; xUnit1051 forces TestContext.Current.CancellationToken on any call with an optional token (including QueryCommand.Prepare).

Test counts (current, after the bug fix): nextorm.core.tests 85/85; nextorm.sqlite.tests 23 total / 0 failed / 0 skipped; nextorm.integration.tests 307 total / 0 failed / 1 skip; Release+Debug builds 0 warnings / 0 errors. Also verified end-to-end that streaming still works: SqliteBenchmarkIteration (all 10 arms incl. Nextorm_Prepared_AsyncStream / Nextorm_Cached_ToListAsync / Dapper_AsyncStream) runs with no exceptions, values consistent with the earlier full run (Prepared_ToListAsync 11.51 us vs 10.78 us - within ShortRun noise).

Diagnostics improvement applied on top of the cache-enumerator bug fix: added `DbContext.RequireEnumerator<TResult>(DbPreparedQueryCommand<TResult>)` which returns `compiledQuery.Enumerator` or throws InvalidOperationException ("This prepared command has no enumerator because it was created with nonStreamUsing: true, which is optimised for buffered and scalar results. Use Prepare(nonStreamUsing: false) to stream (ToAsyncEnumerable/ToEnumerable/CreateEnumerator)."). name: nextorm-issue-27-lob-streaming
observations: Issue #27 LOB streaming (BLOB/CLOB as Stream/TextReader), milestone 1.0.8-b, still open after cycle 2.

Phase 1 (2026-09-27) shipped ToStream/ToStreamAsync/ToTextReader/ToTextReaderAsync on QueryCommand<byte[]>/QueryCommand<string> for PostgreSQL + SQL Server only; other providers throw NotSupportedException.

Core LOB path: DataContext.PrepareLobCommand uses storeInCache:false, no-mapper direct GetStream(0)/GetTextReader(0); CommandBehavior.SequentialAccess gate is ISqlDialect.SupportsSequentialAccess; single-column guard FieldCount!=1 at QueryCommandExtensions.cs:203/223/243/263; no dialect projection hook; select columns assembled in SqlBuilder.cs:455-472; RangeColumnRole/RangeColumns is the only synthetic-role-column precedent.

Cycle 3 (2026-09-27) shipped SQLite binary+text LOB streaming: SqliteDialect overrides SupportsSequentialAccess => true and the new public ISqlDialect.LobLocatorColumn => "rowid" (string?, DIM null; SqlDialectBase virtual null).

Mechanism: QueryPlanner threads sequentialAccess into SqlBuildContext.SequentialAccess; SqlBuilder appends the dialect locator as a trailing select item (SqlBuilder.cs:477) only when !ParamMode && SequentialAccess && LobLocatorColumn != null; payload stays ordinal 0 (GetStream(0)/GetTextReader(0)).

Guard in QueryCommandExtensions.EnsureLobFieldCount: locator dialect + raw WithSql override => FieldCount==1 throws NotSupportedException (rowid locator cannot be added safely), FieldCount!=1 keeps the existing InvalidOperationException; generated SQLite LOB expects 2 fields, others 1.

Fail-closed: view/WITHOUT ROWID raise the raw Microsoft.Data.Sqlite SqliteException ('no such column: rowid'); no buffered fallback; raw WithSql rejected on SQLite. Unsupported shapes (joins/multi-source/DISTINCT/UNION/GROUP BY/aggregates) deferred (bare rowid may error at runtime); trigger = concrete user scenario.

Verified: build 0/0; unit all green; container integration 2105/0 failed (PG/SS/MySQL/ClickHouse ran); coverage line 86.4%/branch 76.8% = baseline; DocFX 0/0; acceptance 7/7 ratio 1.89; SQLite LOB harness bounded (BLOB ~76 KB, CLOB ~145 KB flat at 1/8 MiB).

Cycle 4 (2026-09-27) shipped phase 2 `ToDataReader`/`ToDataReaderAsync` (issue #27). Public terminals on `QueryCommand<TResult>` return a caller-owned forward-only `System.Data.Common.DbDataReader`; new `internal sealed LobDataReader : DbDataReader` in src/nextorm.core/DataContext/LobDataReader.cs owns `CommandReaderOwner` (reader + per-call command) and disposes idempotently. Supported on PostgreSQL + SQL Server only; SQLite is fail-closed (`NotSupportedException`, its rowid locator would add a column to the general reader); MySQL/MariaDB/ClickHouse/in-memory rejected before execution. Gate `EnsureDataReaderSupported` = `SupportsSequentialAccess && LobLocatorColumn is null`.

Planner contract said receiver = non-generic `QueryCommand`, but the whole LOB path (`OpenLobReader<TResult>`/`PrepareLobCommand<TResult>`/`GetPreparedQueryCommand<TResult>`) is generic — there is no non-generic variant. Deviated to generic `QueryCommand<TResult>` (TResult unused; mapper disabled on sequential path) to avoid new internal plumbing (KISS).

Cycle-4 CHECK fixes: (1) both terminals passed an inverted `hideTrailingLocator` arg, dropping a column on PG/SQL Server (integration caught it: IndexOutOfRangeException in CheckOrdinal); (2) removed the speculative hideTrailingLocator seam (no consumer); (3) `LobDataReader.Close()` was a silent no-op contradicting its XML-doc → now releases, guarded against Dispose→Close recursion; (4) ReadAsync/NextResultAsync skip CreateLinkedTokenSource when the open token is not cancelable (removes per-row CTS allocation); (5) generalized the gate diagnostics so ToDataReader names itself, in-memory message no longer enumerates scalar terminals.

name: nextorm CSV streaming (#112)
observations: Provider column mapping in nextorm boxes for SQL Server numerics: SqlServerDataContext.MapColumnExpression reads via IDataRecord.GetValue + Convert.ChangeType (object). A non-shared consumer that must avoid per-row boxing (e.g. the CSV terminal) needs its own provider hook (protected virtual DataContext.MapTypedColumnExpression overridden in SqlServerDataContext) that reads the storage-typed getter (reader.GetFieldType once at bind) plus a typed Convert.To<T>; do not change shared buffered materialization.

Stream terminals that reject unsupported projections must validate columns PRE-EXECUTION from static SelectExpression metadata; binding typed reads after the reader opens (needed for GetFieldType) moves validation too late, so the query executes and surfaces a raw DB error (e.g. missing table) instead of NotSupportedException.

The CSV terminal lives in QueryCommandExtensions/EntityBuilderExtensions (extensions, not QueryCommand<TResult>), uses a new internal plain multi-column reader seam OpenResultReader[Async] (mirroring OpenLobReader without the LOB sequential/locator gates) so it works on SQLite/MySQL/ClickHouse too, prepares with storeInCache:false, and never closes the caller's Stream.

name: PDCA lesson: source-generator typed join aliases (nextorm #113)
observations: A C# source generator can make per-call-site typed alias projections compile with no pre-declared projection by emitting, per discovered alias schema, a concrete projection type with lexical properties plus a [JoinSlot(n)] attribute, and an extension-method overload whose extra parameter is a generated alias marker; the expression visitor resolves the slot from the attribute instead of parsing ItemN digits.
The PoC proved executable slot mapping on SQLite (Buyer=t2.Id, Approver=t3.Id, same CLR type) with 0/0 builds and 1215/1215 core tests.

Ergonomic cost: when the query crosses a method boundary, the user must name the generated type in the method signature (e.g. AliasJoin_Buyer_Approver<Order,Person,Person>), because no per-call-site inference is possible across methods.

Generator constraints observed: full-compilation output (not incremental), no arity cap beyond Projection<T1..T8>, syntax-only alias detection, generated getters that throw if invoked outside expression trees.

name: opencode permission glob write-proof allowlist
observations: In opencode agents, bash permission globs match the whole command and `*` captures spaces, so any `*` before ` -- ` admits appended write flags (e.g. `git diff --no-color --output=/f`, `git log* --output=/f`). For read-only roles use fully literal commands or literal command + ` -- *` (after `--`, tokens are pathspecs). Denylists are bypassable and insufficient.

Verified 2026-10-03 while building the universal stack-agnostic `pdca` skill (config/skills/pdca) from pdca-dotnet: red->green negative-probe unittest proved the old globs matched `--output`; the write-proof form closed it. Residual: shell redirection (`>`, `|`) is not parsed by permission globs and cannot be closed without dropping bash.

name: generated-viewer-token-guard
observations: When a build/generator embeds opaque binary payloads (base64 fonts / data-URIs) into an artifact, a whole-tree text invariant can fail on coincidental substrings; respond with a deterministic structural post-processor (e.g. brace-aware removal of data-URI @font-face rules) plus a fail-closed postcondition, never a hardcoded deny-list, or omit the artifact.

When a whole-tree token/neutrality invariant is coextensive with the deliverable itself, prefer hand-authored, dependency-free assets that satisfy it by construction over generated output that must be scrubbed; an explicitly documented defer with a retry trigger is preferable to faking a non-neutral artifact.

name: opencode agent permission blocks
observations: Read-only / structural subagents in this opencode config are only fail-closed when a top-level `"*": deny` is present in the `permission` block; denying a few named tools is not enough because unlisted tools (grep, glob, webfetch, websearch, list, lsp, MCP) are not otherwise excluded.
A subagent `permission` block must still explicitly allow the one action the role owns (e.g. `todowrite` for an orchestrator/runner) even under a top-level `"*": deny`.
Role/subagent markdown files carry only `# tier: cheap|medium|strong`; concrete model ids belong in the profile `agent` block, never in the role file.

name: pdca-validate-inner-loop-one-sweep-cap
observations: pdca-dotnet helper validate_inner_loop.py caps a report at ONE comprehensive boundary test sweep (an unfiltered `dotnet test`) and ONE boundary solution build (a `dotnet build` referencing `.sln/.slnx`); only filtered boundary tests are uncapped.

A `dotnet run` of a full integration suite is NOT counted by the script as a boundary sweep (`is_test` is false), but a semantic checker may still treat it as an extra comprehensive sweep; do not rely on that loophole.

Reconcile a plan that used several per-project boundary sweeps by making ONE comprehensive full-solution sweep (it subsumes the per-project sweeps) plus ONE boundary solution build; do not relabel or delete the extra historical runs - retain them as history marked excluded/superseded.
An unconditional mandated check (validator exit 0) cannot be waived; a named waiver is rejected. The only valid path is to genuinely re-perform verification in the compliant form.
Proof of container-provider execution can be extracted from the single full-solution sweep's own JUnit/TRX artifact (per-provider test classes), without launching a separate integration run.

name: PDCA transferable lessons

Verify such clauses under BOTH option values (the off/default path is the risky one), and require a red-to-green regression test for the fix.

name: nextorm-PDCA-202-clean-catalog-composite
observations: nextorm integration reuse containers mask clean-catalog bugs: the reused postgres:17-alpine container already had hstore/ltree extensions, so PostgresRawRowTests passed locally while the same tests failed on CI's fresh container. To reproduce, purge the reuse postgres container (podman.exe --connection podman-machine-default rm -f <id>).

Npgsql 10.0.3 on a clean type catalog cannot distinguish an unmapped non-composite (hstore/ltree) from a genuine composite in-memory: GetDataTypeName='-.-', GetFieldType throws InvalidCastException, GetPostgresType=UnknownBackendType (OID 0) for all; only the server OID differs. Npgsql has no MARS, so no second command while a reader is open (NpgsqlOperationInProgressException), and NpgsqlConnection.ReloadTypes() cannot run with an open reader.

Fix pattern used for #202: warm the shared implicit Npgsql data source with a throwaway `new NpgsqlConnection(cs).Open(); conn.ReloadTypes();` after DDL — it affects all string-ctor connections including the context's; `NpgsqlDataSource.Create(cs).ReloadTypes()` does NOT affect the implicit data source used by contexts.

name: Npgsql cold type catalog classification
observations: On a Npgsql connection whose type catalog was loaded before a type existed (clean/cold catalog), an unmapped Postgres type and a genuine composite are indistinguishable: GetDataTypeName returns the Unspecified placeholder "-.-", GetFieldType throws InvalidCastException, and GetPostgresType returns UnknownBackendType (OID 0). Only the wire server OID differs (extension OIDs are not stable).

Authoritative composite detection needs positive evidence: NpgsqlDataReader.GetPostgresType(ordinal) is PostgresCompositeType works only on a warm catalog; on a cold catalog it is UnknownBackendType -> no verdict. Do not infer composite from a dotted data type name or from an exception shape.

NpgsqlDataReader.GetColumnSchema() can be called right after ExecuteReader before Read() without a second command ONLY when CommandBehavior.KeyInfo is absent; with KeyInfo it clones the connection and issues a catalog SELECT under TransactionScope.Suppress (breaks transaction visibility). NpgsqlDataSource.ReloadTypes() opens a new connection, so it cannot see uncommitted types and is unsuitable when classifying on the open reader.

Design consequence used in nextorm #203: classify composite via one provider seam (protected DataContext.IsGenuineCompositeColumn -> Npgsql override), share it by single- and multi-column raw-row paths, and accept that a cold-catalog genuine composite degrades to the ordinary mapping error instead of a misleading named-composite diagnostic.

name: PDCA-host-constraints-opencode-config
observations: In this host (opencode-config), the `pdca-check` role has no file-read access and judges only the aggregated brief; every CHECK brief must be fully self-contained with verbatim evidence + file:line pointers, otherwise criteria return `unverified` purely for missing-report reasons.

The `pdca-orchestrator` agent is absent here; autonomous `pdca` cycles run via the flat cheap-primary fallback (log a Notice:), and there is no `todowrite` tool, so the sidebar todo mirror cannot be maintained.

For document/engineering-design deliverables under `pdca`, most failed CHECKs were brief-evidence gaps or presentation inconsistencies, not physical/calculation defects; escalation→replan→fix converged at r=4 with 3 escalations for the egg-drop task.

name: PDCA re-entry after terminal incomplete
observations: A redo after a terminal incomplete/STOP must not re-run the failed decisive criterion unchanged: either demonstrate the proof is now obtainable or re-scope to a reproducible oracle.

A decisive-evidence probe's obtainability against the declared baseline must be demonstrated (reconnaissance) BEFORE plan_state=ready; a declared source whose probe cannot run on baseline is a GAP, not ready.

The reusable delta of a diverged preserved branch is git diff <merge-base> <branch-tip> (branch-owned work), NOT git diff <current-HEAD> <branch-tip> (which reflects unrelated newer work as deletions).

name: Evidence freshness and oracle integrity in PDCA
observations: A green↔green invariant oracle must be genuinely cross-tree (baseline capture vs revised capture + diff), not a self-consistent write-then-read test; a decisive oracle also needs demonstrated discrimination (red-on-perturb).

The comprehensive boundary evidence must be re-run after the LAST product change: retained green runs that predate a later fix are an evidence-freshness blocker, not a pass (no product defect required to fail CHECK).
CHECK can fail purely on evidence completeness/reconciliation; that is re-gathered (evidence-only loop-back), not counted as a product-defect iteration.

name: pdca-oracle-reentry-lessons
observations: PDCA re-entry after a terminal incomplete: a criterion whose decisive oracle is unreachable-by-construction must be re-scoped to a reproducible oracle OR preserved as an explicit GAP ledger entry (status open, with file:line proof and a reopen trigger) — never re-run the unsatisfiable fixture unchanged. Keep GAP rows OUT of the cycle's PASS-blocking required_rows, otherwise the evidence contract deadlocks (an open row cannot PASS).

PDCA oracle strength: assertions like count==1 or empty==empty can pass vacuously. Pair the collapse/count assertion with an independent positive control proving all inputs were processed (e.g. distinct-alias variant yielding exactly two methods), and assert expected declarations are present before any byte comparison; demonstrate the negative (removing an input/declaration makes the test fail).

name: T209 eager-load strategy (nextorm #209)
observations: nextorm collection 1.0.9-todo lane G1, task T209 (#209): eager-load strategy — explicit EagerLoadMode + context default (UseEagerLoadMode) + conservative Auto->SplitQuery + fail-closed Correlated/per-parent top-N + structural plan-cache identity (EagerLoadShape).

Result: done. N=1, r=3, n=2/3, evidence contract rv=2; CHECK PASS. Commits on branch 1.0.9 from d12b740e: ed9ac341..2700a59c (r1 impl/tests), d69e6569 (top-N pre-SQL), 369830fd..f90ffee3 (docs/perf/manifest), 8bdcee2a/0b642c50 (r2 F1/F2/F3/F4), dd5d08fb (terminal/list JoinInto guard), 68828204/886be17d (rv2 boundary), 5e9f6756/8829f3e4 (r3 wording+boundary), 4b50672f/aa6b548c (required tests), 2b337021/8b771a7b (ACT). Issue #209 closed.

Lesson 1 (fail-closed guard placement): an unsupported-strategy/top-N guard must run at EVERY dispatch entry — plain split, list-JoinInto, AND every non-list terminal (ToParentCommand/SelectParent) — before command build/cache/SQL; restoring baseline mixed JoinInto+LoadWith dispatch without adding the guard to that branch reintroduced a fail-open (R209-05) defect.

Lesson 2 (declarative detection limit): per-parent child paging (Limit/Offset/Page) is only observable on the built EntityBuilder (EntityBuilder.Paging), because LoadWith takes Func<IDataContext,EntityBuilder<TChild>> with no declarative metadata; any top-N rejection must therefore invoke the user child factory. Resolve by declaring it: factory invoked at most once per (spec, context), memoized, must be pure/idempotent.

Lesson 3 (PDCA): when a CHECK FAIL is driven by evidence provenance rather than a demonstrated product defect, recover evidence (pinned baseline coverage, changed-branch map, terminal-surface audit, suppression counters) rather than iterating DO; Stryker on nextorm.core is toolchain-blocked (Safe-Mode CS0165, coverage Dubious) per repo precedent.

name: pdca-evidence-capture
observations: PDCA/CHECK evidence: mandatory commands must be run through a direct-child capture wrapper that records the child's real exit code / signal / timeout; never infer exit codes from downstream artifacts (e.g. a report JSON existing).

A receipt showing exit_code=0 can be a race when the wrapper killed the child on timeout (SIGTERM/SIGKILL): the wrapper must return nonzero on timeout and the timeout flag must take precedence over any zero child exit. Validate the race with a short controlled SIGTERM-ignoring process before expensive runs.

Evidence rows must bind to a single consistent campaign identity: the captured log/receipt and any retained native exports must come from the SAME run (matching measurement values), otherwise the row is not substantiated even if paths/hashes resolve.
A test asserting an ordering must include a structural assertion on the emitted SQL, not only result equality: a lucky database order can otherwise mask an omitted ordering.

name: Stryker.NET mutant statuses in triage
observations: In Stryker.NET reports a mutant status of `Pending` means 'not fully tested' (typically a runner-session timeout / the mutant was never activated under MTP parallelism) — it is NOT `Survived`. Conflating the two turns an evidence gap into a false product defect.

A `NoCoverage` mutant is also distinct: it means no test in the configured test-projects covered the mutant, so a mutant on a line whose coverage XML reports hits>=1 can still be NoCoverage/Pending if the mutation run's test selection differed from the coverage run's.

Mutation scores are only comparable when coverage-analysis is on (perTest) and the same test-runner is used; a run with coverage-analysis disabled can report 0.00% with all mutants Survived and is meaningless.
Disposition every survivor explicitly (killed / equivalent / outside-diff / covered-by-other-project / unresolved-with-reason) and never present a NoCoverage branch as covered.

name: PDCA long-running evidence commands
observations: Long-running evidence commands (container integration suites, instrumented coverage sweeps, benchmark runs) must be dispatched as their own single-command invocation; bundling several long commands or a scripted sweep into one subagent call tends to overrun the agent step/wall budget and returns a partial report.

When a coverage gate is defined over a CI sweep, reproduce the CI test-selection scope (whole-solution test run) rather than only the included modules' own suites, otherwise aggregate percentages are understated and look like a false regression.

name: WSL port forward 3031 -> 3030 (WebPDCA)
observations: Windows 127.0.0.1:3031 is bridged to a service listening on 127.0.0.1:3030 inside WSL by a PowerShell TCP forwarder script: C:\Users\user\wsl-forward.ps1 (it prints 'WebPDCA forwarder: 127.0.0.1:<ListenPort> -> <TargetHost>:<TargetPort>').
Launch command (run from WSL; invokes Windows PowerShell): powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\Users\user\wsl-forward.ps1 -ListenPort 3031 -TargetPort 3030
The script defaults are ListenPort=3001, TargetHost=127.0.0.1, TargetPort=3000; the live instance overrides ListenPort=3031 and TargetPort=3030.

It is a raw TcpListener/TcpClient byte pump on IPAddress.Loopback: no netsh portproxy is involved (`netsh interface portproxy show all` is empty). It listens only on Windows 127.0.0.1, so open http://127.0.0.1:3031/ from Windows, not from inside WSL.
Prerequisite: the target app must be listening on port 3030 inside WSL (`ss -ltnp | grep 3030`). The forwarder only relays bytes; if 3030 is down, connections to 3031 hang/time out.

Verify the forwarder from Windows: `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 3031 -State Listen` shows powershell.exe, and `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "ProcessId=<pid>"` shows CommandLine `... -File C:\Users\user\wsl-forward.ps1 -ListenPort 3031 -TargetPort 3030`.

On 2026-10-17 the running forwarder was Windows PID 27140: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\Users\user\wsl-forward.ps1 -ListenPort 3031 -TargetPort 3030 (WSL side 3030 was not listening at that moment).
If the forwarder is missing, start it detached from WSL with the launch command above, then verify with Get-NetTCPConnection; no admin rights are needed because it binds Windows loopback only.

name: WSL Slidev → браузер Windows
observations: Chromium-браузеры (Edge, Yandex) на этой машине не подключаются к серверу, слушающему внутри WSL, хотя curl.exe и Test-NetConnection с Windows проходят (WSL mirrored networking). Ошибка в Edge: ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT.

Рабочая схема: в WSL запустить `npx slidev --remote --port 3030` в docs/ru/pdca-slides, а Windows-форвардер C:\Users\user\wsl-forward.ps1 -ListenPort 3031 -TargetPort 3030 пробрасывает 127.0.0.1:3031 на 127.0.0.1:3030. Браузер открывает http://127.0.0.1:3031/.
Форвардер — TcpListener на 127.0.0.1:listen, переливает байты в 127.0.0.1:target; процесс был запущен 14.10.2026 и висит постоянно.

Если убить dev-сервер Slidev на 3030, порт 3031 продолжает слушать, но соединения падают (curl.exe: http=000). Проверка: `curl.exe -s -o NUL -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3031/` должен вернуть 200.

Открыть в браузере: `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "Start-Process 'msedge.exe' -ArgumentList 'http://127.0.0.1:3031/'"`. Yandex Browser (browser.exe --single-argument <url>) URL из командной строки не подхватывает и открывает пустую вкладку.

Альтернатива, тоже проверенная: `npm run build` в docs/ru/pdca-slides + раздача dist PowerShell-HttpListener'ом на стороне Windows (127.0.0.1:3050) — Chromium её видит, скриншот headless Edge подтвердил рендер. Годится, когда dev-сервер не нужен.
Headless-проверка рендера без показа окна: msedge.exe --headless=new --disable-gpu --window-size=1280,800 --virtual-time-budget=15000 --screenshot=<path> <url>.

name: npm staged publishing (AlexeyShirshov/skills)
observations: Repo https://github.com/AlexeyShirshov/skills publishes npm plugins from opencode/plugins/<name> (wsl-notify, opencode-roslyn). Flow is npm STAGED publishing: the release is first staged, then a maintainer approves it with 2FA (npmjs.com or `npm stage approve <id>`); nothing lands on the registry unreviewed.
`npm stage` needs npm >= 11.5.1. The machine's local npm is 10.x (no `stage` command), so always call it as `npx --yes npm@latest stage publish` / `stage list` / `stage approve <id>`.

Auth: a valid `_authToken` in ~/.npmrc for https://registry.npmjs.org. Sanity check before staging: `npx --yes npm@latest whoami` must print `alexeyshirshov`. E401 = expired/invalid token, must be refreshed (npm login or a new token) before staging.

Never use version `0.0.0-stage`: since Oct 2026 it is npm's own placeholder for `npm stage publish` of a package that does not exist yet, and the registry rejects it for an ordinary publish. Always use a real version.

opencode-roslyn is staged BY CI: .github/workflows/publish-npm.yml triggers on tags `opencode-roslyn-v*`, uses OIDC trusted publishing (default stage-only rights), and fails if the tag version != package.json version; then the human runs `npx --yes npm@latest stage approve <id>`.

wsl-notify has NO CI staging (the workflow only matches opencode-roslyn tags), so it is staged manually: `cd opencode/plugins/wsl-notify && npx --yes npm@latest stage publish`, then the human approves the printed stage id.

Release record convention: bump `version` in the plugin's package.json, run its smoke test, commit `chore(<package>): <version> — <summary>`, create an ANNOTATED tag `<package>@<version>` (e.g. wsl-notify@1.0.5) with message `<package> <version> — <summary>`, push main and the tag. Tags use the `<package>@<version>` form (npm-style @), unlike CI packages which use `opencode-roslyn-v<version>`.
Verify after approval: `npx --yes npm@latest stage list` shows the stage entry; the registry `dist-tags.latest` for the package must equal the new version (curl https://registry.npmjs.org/<package>).

Published tarball contents come only from package.json `files`; for the plugins that is index.js, README.md, LICENSE (+ package.json). Tests, .pdca/ evidence logs and docs outside `files` are not published.

After approval the stage entry disappears from `npm stage list` ('No staged packages found') and the version shows up in the registry `versions` map with a `time` entry; compare its `dist.shasum` with the staged shasum to prove the approved tarball is the published one.

STAGING NEEDS NO 2FA/OTP — that is the whole point: `npx --yes npm@latest stage publish` completes with the token alone (verified 2026-10-20 on opencode-git-status-v1: staged with no OTP prompt, stage id 9faa28f5-3b06-4204-9bfd-959025d3a1a5). 2FA is only for APPROVAL (`npx --yes npm@latest stage approve <id>` or the package page). A plain `npm publish` is the wrong command for this repo and DOES demand an OTP (fails with EOTP). Never ask the user for an OTP before staging, and never suggest plain `npm publish`.

name: git commit hygiene in skills repo

name: opencode-config: switch cheap tier to direct DeepSeek
observations: Tier→model ids live ONLY in the profile `agent` block (`config/profiles/<profile>.jsonc`); `agents/*.md`, docs and skills carry only `# tier: cheap|medium|strong`.

In `deepseek.jsonc` (alias oc-ds) the cheap tier = `pdca-orchestrator`, `pdca-executor`, `coder`, `scout`. `btw` is also cheap but is not part of the PDCA cycle, and the default top-level `"model"` (interactive build/plan session) is a separate binding — neither is switched together with the cheap tier unless the user explicitly asks.

Model ids for the switch: Go-subscription cheap = `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`; direct DeepSeek cheap = `deepseek/deepseek-flash` (same id as `small_model`). Switching cheap off the Go quota = replace the model in the four cheap roles and update the tier comment above the `agent` block.

Deploy path for a profile edit: edit the snapshot in the repo → `bun config/tools/sync-profiles.mjs --check` (prints per-role drift) → `--fix` (refuses files with local edits; `--force` overrides). Never edit `~/.config/opencode/profiles/` directly.

No opencode restart is needed: V2 watches config (packages/core/src/config.ts → Config.reload, 100 ms debounce → `config.updated`; config/plugin/agent.ts → ctx.agent.reload()). Confirm in ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log as `event.type=config.updated event.location.directory=<dir>`.

Hot-reload scope: already-spawned subagents finish on the model they started with; new subagents resolve `agent.model` at spawn; the primary session is pinned via `session.model` and is NOT overridden by agent bindings.

Project `opencode.json` merges after the profile: explicit bindings win; project agents that only have a `# tier:` comment and no binding inherit the default `"model"` and therefore stay on whatever the default is (in nextorm that kept cheap project agents on Go). Project worktrees have their own committed copy of `opencode.json`, so an uncommitted edit in the main tree does not reach sessions started in a worktree.
Foreign repos (e.g. /home/alex/sources/nextorm) are edited only with explicit user permission, and never committed without an explicit request.
